about: The balance gate's bands (tools/balance-check.mjs). Each band records what the game IS - measured on 120 to 500 seeds in docs/lab/ladder-2026-09-18.md - with room for a 40-seed sample. A band is moved in the PR that means to move the game, and its `why` says so.

bands.why: A player who knows nothing - one plain Bolt by the entry, then nothing - holds Calm's wave 5. The stranger test plays Calm to wave 5 unaided. Measured 99.6% of 500.
...and then loses, having seen the game: a first run that cannot be lost teaches nothing. Measured 1.8% of 500 win.
The base world's reference, going on buying, wins Calm. Measured 100% of 500.
Three plain Bolts by the entry and nothing more do not win Standard. Measured 0% of 120.
The reference, going on, wins Standard most of the time. Measured 97.4% of 500.

NOT a player: the six-tower reference that stops buying, played to wave 40. It dies mid-run, so its mean death wave moves with the smallest change to a curve, a price or a road, where the win rates above sit near 100% and do not move. Measured 25.20 over 80; the band is half a wave either side.
The same thermometer on Grim. Measured 21.85 over 80. Proven on 2026-09-18: Grim's growth nudged x1.09 -> x1.10 read 20.95 (RED) while Grim's win rate went 94% -> 91% and stayed inside its band.

NOT a target met: L5 says the base world should LOSE Grim, and it wins 93.6% of 500. The band records what is, so that a change to Grim's curve is a red check and a decision, not a drift. See the call in docs/lab/ladder-2026-09-18.md.
